newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends lower on fund liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends lower on fund liquidation.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended lower for the third consecutive session Monday, pressured by fund liquidation, traders said.
But volume was thin at an estimated 5,273 lots, and trading subdued with the London cocoa futures market closed for a holiday. The LCE will resume trading on Tuesday.

The benchmark December cocoa settled down $9 a tonne, at $1,382, its lowest level in three weeks, and just above the session low of $1,380. December's high was $1,390. Spot September fell $21, to $1,329, while the back months closed $2 to $13 lower.
Dealers said steady scale-down trade buying stemmed losses and held prices to a narrow range.
Technically, traders pegged December support at $1,377, with the subsequent level seen at $1,360. Resistance was seen at $1,405-$1,408, a gap on the charts formed on Friday.

Traders still await fresh crop assessments from the Ivory Coast for fundamental direction. Talk that revised pod counts for the 1996/97 havest would come in at around 900,000 tonne, a bit higher than earlier estimates, may have weighed on prices, traders said.
